Several high-cardinality categoricals (industry cardinality 31, language cardinality 27, payment_method cardinality 23, acquisition_channel cardinality 19) compound the problem, since imputing 14-22% of values in wide-category columns is risky. Three numeric columns also show a sentinel-like extreme of 9999.0 (balance max, session_minutes max, discount_rate max) against means around 127, suggesting missing-value placeholders that must be recoded before imputation. Clean columns exist (credit_score, page_views, is_active, signup_date all at missing_pct 0.0), so a defensible path is to drop or carefully encode the sparse categoricals and treat the 9999 sentinels as missing. Given the volume of missing data and the sentinel contamination, cleaning is warranted before training.

The dataset is not ready to train as-is. It has 1200 rows and 24 columns, with a binary target (cardinality 2, roughly 69/31 imbalance), so the task itself is well-posed. The blocker is missingness: 265 missing values in industry (22.08%) is the most affected column, followed by language (234 missing, 19.5%), payment_method (167, 13.92%), acquisition_channel (152, 12.67%), device_type (100, 8.33%), referral_count (103, 8.58%) and balance (102, 8.5%). These are all in the 8-22% band, which is too large to ignore and too large for naive listwise deletion on a 1200-row dataset — a model would either lose a substantial fraction of rows or be fitted on a non-representative subsample. The high-cardinality categoricals (industry 31, language 27, payment_method 23, acquisition_channel 19, device_type 15) compound this: imputing them with a mode or a constant would be both biased and nearly meaningless, and some categories may not survive cleaning at all. Separately, balance, session_minutes and discount_rate share a max of exactly 9999.0 with markedly inflated standard deviations (846.24, 828.49, 824.59 respectively) and 8 z-score outliers each — a classic sentinel-value pattern that should be recoded to missing rather than treated as data. Note that credit_score, page_views, is_active and signup_date are fully populated, so a reduced but clean feature set is achievable. Recommendation: recover or drop the sentinel-9999 values first, then choose an explicit imputation strategy per column (e.g. drop or consolidate sparse categories for the high-cardinality nominals, median imputation for numerics) before any training run.
